messages:
alex: heads-up: the driver/CUDA push to 542.01 hit a compatibility regression on eu-west H100 pools. tensorrt / flashattn kernels failing during eager exec on several services. rolling canary showed errors on model-serving pods.

priya: details? which stacks and what error? did canary hit dedicated or shared nodes? :eyes:

alex: canary was on dedicated-gpu-eu-1, TRT 8.5.2 + flashattn 1.0.2 + xformers built from main. error sample pasted from pod logs:

```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:913] failed to load PTX module: ptx compilation failed: unsupported ptx version 7.x for device sm_8xx
E tensorrt: plugin failure: cuModuleLoadDataEx() -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_STATE
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/app/serve.py", line 214, in forward
    out = flash_attn_cuda.forward(q, k, v)
RuntimeError: NVRTC: ptx lower failed: PTX verification failed
```

alex: same job on us-west with older driver (541.22) is fine.

daniel: PV: looks like NVRTC/PTX codegen mismatch with new driver+CUDA combo. xformers/flashattn used precompiled kernels targeting ptx 7.5, new driver enforces stricter verifier for LTO/relocations.

daniel: quick triage notes: 1) building flashattn/xformers with CUDA 12.2 toolchain and explicit -arch=sm_90 might help; 2) TRT could be loading precompiled PTX blobs that are now rejected.

emily: we should pause the rollout. rollback plan? how many nodes affected?

sebastian: infra count: 42 H100 nodes in eu-west on the new driver; ~18% of eu region capacity for inference. Canary (2/5 pods) failed p95 latency and saw 10--15% error rate.

infra-bot: [canary-metrics] eu-west-dedicated-gpu-1: 2/5 pods failing, error-rate 12.4%, p95 latency +230ms vs baseline.

deploy-bot: automatic rollout paused at step 3 due to policy: failure-threshold exceeded.

priya: action: roll back drivers on the 5 canary hosts first, then hold global. alex / infra-ops can you run the rollback?

alex: starting rollback on canaries now. command used:
```
ssh admin@dedicated-eu-01 'sudo apt-get install --allow-downgrades nvidia-driver-541=541.22 -y && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-serving -n prod-eu
```

emily: after rollback one canary pod came back healthy. need a postmortem and NV ticket.

daniel: for mitigation we can also rebuild flashattn with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0;8.6;9.0` and set NVRTC flags to generate compatible PTX rather than embedded cubin. that will be safer but takes build+validation time.

priya: assign owners: alex infra-ops = rollback + reconcile, daniel eng-ml = build/repro, emily = customer comms + impact tracking, priya = NV vendor escalation.

alex: opened internal ticket with NV (INC-4823) and attached logs + PTX. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4823

sebastian: cost note: if we hold drivers back, Dedicated upgrade window will slip. flagged for PMs.

daniel: FYI, difference here is verifier tightened in 542.x for PTX version selection; many third-party libs that bundled prebuilt PTX are failing. recommend we add a canary step: scan images for bundled PTX/cubin and rebuild or set nvrtc to runtime compile.

emily: customer-facing note drafted: short incident summary, implications, ETA for full resolution = TBD. will post on status page if any customer-visible errors persist.

priya: thanks — plan for next 4 hours: 1) rollback canaries completed (alex), 2) hold global rollout (infra), 3) eng-ml to produce repro build (daniel), 4) open vendor escalation (priya). update this thread with progress. :thumbsup:
